name: Septon 40mm f/2 Aspherical, Sony E
released: 2026-02-13 (announced); shipping spring 2026 (PetaPixel: March; Newsshooter: April in Japan)
contacts: yes: EXIF, focus-ring-triggered magnification and peaking/frame-colour focus aids, distance encoder so 5-axis IBIS gets focus distance
notes: Drew's ~30 mm is exactly right for E. Known weaknesses in reviews: corner softness and CA wide open, vignetting, some flare (sonyalpha.blog, Fred Miranda). Voigtländer lists LH-14/LH-15 hoods as optional for E; hood/cap add length not counted here. Phoblographer raised a Sony-licence worry after Viltrox lenses failed on the a7 V; they note Cosina has held the licence since 2011 and no failure was reported.

name: Septon 40mm f/2 Aspherical, Nikon Z
lengthMeasured: from the mount flange (Voigtländer; Newsshooter '32mm from mount flange')
contacts: yes: EXIF, focus aids (frame colour, peaking, magnification button), 3-axis IBIS info per Newsshooter
notes: Correction to Drew's figure: the Z version is 32 mm, not 30, and 40 g heavier (205 g), with a wider 68.3 mm barrel and scalloped focus ring. Voigtländer says the Z version ships with a screw-on dome hood.

name: Lumix S 40mm f/2 (S-S40)
lengthMeasured: Panasonic 'overall length', which on Lumix S spec sheets is tip of lens to base side of the mount
notes: PRIMARY L-mount pairing (Drew's pick). Drew's 'about 40 mm' is right: 40.9 mm, so it sticks out about 11 mm more than the E Septon. Dust/splash/freeze (-10 C) resistant, fluorine front element, no OIS. Reviews: sharp centre wide open, minor corner softness until f/4, notable longitudinal CA (PetaPixel). DPReview calls it more muffin than pancake. Same 40.9 mm length and 62 mm filter as the 20mm f/2.5 and the 18-40mm kit zoom.
